titulo: How Will Technology Change Us? Grammar and Technoethics in the Future
titulo_es: ¿Cómo nos cambiará la tecnología? Gramática y tecnoética del futuro
estandares: Describo con precisión personas, objetos y procesos, y comparo alternativas. Hago proyecciones sobre el futuro tecnológico y evalúo sus implicaciones.
competencias: Distinguir adjetivos de adverbios; usar will y going to para proyectar el futuro; comparar y jerarquizar con comparativos y superlativos; discutir tecnología y tecnoética.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada grupo presenta una proyección del año 2050 en un ámbito (educación, salud, transporte): qué habrá cambiado, qué será mejor o peor que hoy y qué límites éticos deberían fijarse.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each group presents a projection of the year 2050 in one field (education, health, transport): what will have changed, what will be better or worse than today and what ethical limits should be set.

lecciones.content_es:
Qué describe cada uno

  • Adjetivo → describe un sustantivo: a quick answer
  • Adverbio → describe un verbo, un adjetivo u otro adverbio: He answered quickly

Formación

Adjetivo + -ly: careful → carefully. Consonante + y → -ily: easy → easily. Termina en -le → -ly: possible → possibly.

Irregulares y trampas

  • good → well · fast → fast · hard → hard
  • hardly NO es el adverbio de hard: significa «apenas». I hardly slept = casi no dormí.
  • Con verbos de percepción (look, feel, smell, sound, taste, seem) va adjetivo: It looks good, no looks well.

Orden

El adverbio de modo suele ir después del verbo o del objeto: She explained the topic clearly.
lecciones.content_en:
What each one describes

  • Adjective → describes a noun: a quick answer
  • Adverb → describes a verb, an adjective or another adverb: He answered quickly

Formation

Adjective + -ly: careful → carefully. Consonant + y → -ily: easy → easily. Ending in -le → -ly: possible → possibly.

Irregulars and traps

  • good → well · fast → fast · hard → hard
  • hardly is NOT the adverb of hard: it means "barely". I hardly slept = I almost did not sleep.
  • With perception verbs (look, feel, smell, sound, taste, seem) use an adjective: It looks good, not looks well.

Order

The manner adverb usually goes after the verb or the object: She explained the topic clearly.

lecciones.t: Futuro con will y going to
lecciones.t_en: Future with will and going to
lecciones.content_es:
La elección

  • will – predicción por opinión, decisión del momento, promesa: AI will change education.
  • going to – plan previo o predicción con evidencia: They're going to launch the app next month.

Grados de certeza

It will definitely happen. · It will probably happen. · It might happen. · It probably won't happen.

El adverbio va después de will y antes de won't.

Futuro continuo y perfecto

  • will be + -ing – acción en curso en un momento futuro: By 2050 we will be using autonomous cars.
  • will have + participio – acción terminada antes de un momento futuro: By 2050 AI will have replaced many tasks.

Ojo

Después de when, before, after, as soon as no va will: When technology improves, costs will drop.
lecciones.content_en:
The choice

  • will – prediction from opinion, on-the-spot decision, promise: AI will change education.
  • going to – prior plan or prediction with evidence: They're going to launch the app next month.

Degrees of certainty

It will definitely happen. · It will probably happen. · It might happen. · It probably won't happen.

The adverb goes after will and before won't.

Future continuous and perfect

  • will be + -ing – an action in progress at a future moment: By 2050 we will be using autonomous cars.
  • will have + participle – an action finished before a future moment: By 2050 AI will have replaced many tasks.

Careful

After when, before, after, as soon as there is no will: When technology improves, costs will drop.

lecciones.content_es:
Formas

  • Cortos: -er + than — faster than, cheaper than
  • Consonante + y: -ier — easier than
  • Largos: more … than — more efficient than
  • Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse, far → further

Comparación de igualdad y de inferioridad

  • as … as: This model is as fast as that one.
  • not as … as: It isn't as expensive as I thought.
  • less … than: less complicated than

Intensificar

much faster, far more efficient, a lot cheaper, slightly better, a bit heavier.

Cambio progresivo

Technology is getting faster and faster. · The more we automate, the less we control.
lecciones.content_en:
Forms

  • Short: -er + than — faster than, cheaper than
  • Consonant + y: -ier — easier than
  • Long: more … than — more efficient than
  • Irregular: good → better, bad → worse, far → further

Equality and inferiority

  • as … as: This model is as fast as that one.
  • not as … as: It isn't as expensive as I thought.
  • less … than: less complicated than

Intensifiers

much faster, far more efficient, a lot cheaper, slightly better, a bit heavier.

Progressive change

Technology is getting faster and faster. · The more we automate, the less we control.

lecciones.content_es:
Formas

  • Cortos: the -est — the fastest, the biggest
  • Consonante + y: the -iest — the easiest
  • Largos: the most — the most advanced
  • Irregulares: the best, the worst, the least, the most

Complementos

  • in + lugar o grupo cerrado: the largest company in the world
  • of + conjunto de elementos: the fastest of the three
  • Con presente perfecto: the best film I've ever seen

Ordinales con superlativo

the second largest city · the third most popular app.

Ojo

El artículo the es obligatorio y no se combina most con -est: the most fastest es incorrecto.
lecciones.content_en:
Forms

  • Short: the -est — the fastest, the biggest
  • Consonant + y: the -iest — the easiest
  • Long: the most — the most advanced
  • Irregular: the best, the worst, the least, the most

Complements

  • in + place or closed group: the largest company in the world
  • of + a set of items: the fastest of the three
  • With the present perfect: the best film I've ever seen

Ordinals with superlatives

the second largest city · the third most popular app.

Careful

The article the is compulsory and most is never combined with -est: the most fastest is wrong.

lecciones.content_es:
Tecnología actual

artificial intelligence, algorithm, automation, robotics, machine learning, big data, virtual reality, renewable energy, biotechnology, self-driving car.

Tecnoética

privacy, surveillance (vigilancia), bias (sesgo), digital divide (brecha digital), misinformation, cybersecurity, data protection, transparency, accountability, sustainability.

Impactos

  • Positivos: improve access, save time, reduce costs, connect people, detect diseases early.
  • Negativos: replace jobs, invade privacy, spread misinformation, increase inequality.

Discutirlo

The main advantage is… · A major drawback is… · We need clear rules to prevent… · Who is responsible if…?

lecciones.t: El alfabeto y la precisión técnica
lecciones.content_es:
Deletrear sin ambigüedad

Cuando una letra se puede confundir (B/V, M/N, E/I), se usa una palabra de referencia: B as in Boy, V as in Victor. El alfabeto fonético internacional usa Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta…

Términos técnicos frecuentes

URL, Wi-Fi, PDF, USB, AI, IT, OS — las siglas se deletrean letra por letra.

Símbolos

@ at · # hash · . dot · / slash · _ underscore · - hyphen · & ampersand.

Frases de precisión

All lowercase, no spaces. · That's with a capital W. · Double S. · Is that B as in Boy or V as in Victor?
lecciones.content_en:
Spelling without ambiguity

When a letter can be confused (B/V, M/N, E/I), use a reference word: B as in Boy, V as in Victor. The international phonetic alphabet uses Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta…

Frequent technical terms

URL, Wi-Fi, PDF, USB, AI, IT, OS — acronyms are spelled letter by letter.

Symbols

@ at · # hash · . dot · / slash · _ underscore · - hyphen · & ampersand.

Accuracy phrases

All lowercase, no spaces. · That's with a capital W. · Double S. · Is that B as in Boy or V as in Victor?

repaso.titulo: Repaso — How Will Technology Change Us?
repaso.titulo_en: Review — How Will Technology Change Us?
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Para proyectar el futuro necesitas describir con precisión (adjetivo vs adverbio), proyectar (will, going to, futuro continuo y perfecto) y comparar (comparativos y superlativos).

Puntos gramaticales

  • Adjetivo describe sustantivos; adverbio describe verbos. hardly ≠ hard.
  • Los verbos de percepción (look, sound, feel) llevan adjetivo.
  • will have + participio = terminado antes de una fecha futura.
  • much/far intensifican el comparativo; very no.
  • El superlativo siempre lleva the; in con lugares, of con conjuntos.

Vocabulario

Tecnología (algorithm, automation, machine learning), tecnoética (bias, surveillance, digital divide) y deletreo técnico con referencias de letra.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

To project the future you need to describe precisely (adjective vs adverb), project (will, going to, future continuous and perfect) and compare (comparatives and superlatives).

Grammar points

  • Adjectives describe nouns; adverbs describe verbs. hardly ≠ hard.
  • Perception verbs (look, sound, feel) take an adjective.
  • will have + participle = finished before a future date.
  • much/far intensify a comparative; very does not.
  • The superlative always takes the; in with places, of with sets.

Vocabulary

Technology (algorithm, automation, machine learning), technoethics (bias, surveillance, digital divide) and technical spelling with letter references.
